risk: Front desk staff manipulate reservations, comps and petty cash, and the loss is hidden by the volume of small transactions.
audit_objective: Identify cash and revenue loss at the property and assess whether property-level monitoring detects it.
what_to_review: Comp, discount and rate-override authority at the front desk
Room moves and reservation cancellations after check-in
Petty cash and float custody
Paid-out and refund transactions
Night audit independence
procedures: Analyse comps, rate overrides and zero-rate stays by agent and shift; select the outlier tail for evidence of authorisation.
Test reservations cancelled after the guest checked in, which can conceal a cash sale.
Count floats unannounced at a sample of properties and agree to the recorded balance.
Test paid-outs and refunds for supporting documentation and guest signature.
Confirm the night auditor is not the same person who operated the desk during the shift audited.
red_flags: Comps concentrated on one agent or shift
Repeated room moves to lower rate codes
Floats counted only by their own custodian
Guest folios adjusted after checkout

risk: Property managers direct purchasing to connected suppliers at inflated prices, outside the group procurement framework.
audit_objective: Assess whether property-level purchasing follows the group framework and whether supplier relationships are arm's length.
what_to_review: Use of contracted group suppliers versus local purchasing
Local supplier onboarding and vetting
Price benchmarking against group contracts
Conflict of interest declarations at property level
Splitting of purchases below approval thresholds
procedures: Quantify spend outside the group contracted supplier list by property and category.
Compare unit prices paid locally against the group contract rate for the same items.
Match local supplier details against employee records for shared addresses, phone numbers and bank accounts.
Test for purchase orders split into amounts just below the approval threshold.
red_flags: A property with unusually high local spend
Suppliers created and used only by one property
Invoices consistently just below the threshold
No competitive quotes on recurring local spend
evidence: Accounts payable spend by property and supplier

risk: Pricing and promotion errors are published to the site and honoured at scale before anyone notices, or promotional terms are not met.
audit_objective: Assess control over what is published to customers and how quickly errors are detected and corrected.
what_to_review: Price and promotion change approval before publication
Automated checks on price change magnitude
Stacking of promotions and discount codes
Speed of detection and rollback
Advertising and claims compliance
procedures: Test the approval trail for a sample of price and promotion changes published in the period.
Review automated tolerance checks on price changes and test whether they blocked or flagged extreme values.
Test whether discount codes can be stacked or reused beyond their intended limit by re-performing a checkout in a test environment.
Measure elapsed time from publication of known pricing errors to correction, and quantify orders honoured.
red_flags: Discount codes shared publicly and still active
Price changes published outside working hours without approval
Repeat incidents with the same root cause
No monetary tolerance on automated price feeds

risk: Personal data is retained longer than permitted, shared with third parties without a lawful basis, or exposed through weak access control.
audit_objective: Determine whether personal data is held, used and shared in line with privacy obligations and consent.
what_to_review: Data inventory and lawful basis for each processing purpose
Consent capture and withdrawal handling
Retention and deletion in practice, not just in policy
Third-party data sharing and processor agreements
Access to production customer data by staff and vendors
procedures: Trace a sample of processing purposes to a documented lawful basis and to what customers were actually told.
Test deletion by selecting accounts that requested erasure and searching all systems, including backups and analytics, for residual data.
Reconcile third parties receiving customer data to signed processor agreements.
Review who holds access to production customer data and test whether that access is justified by role.
red_flags: Marketing to customers who withdrew consent
Data retained "in case it is useful"
Analytics tools receiving identifiable data
Vendor access never reviewed after onboarding

subprocess: Route to Market and Distributor Performance
risk: Distributors sell outside their assigned territory, hold stock beyond shelf life, or claim promotional support they did not deliver.
audit_objective: Assess whether distributor arrangements are performing as contracted and claims are substantiated.
what_to_review: Territory assignment and cross-territory selling
Distributor stock levels and shelf-life exposure
Promotional claim substantiation
Credit exposure and payment performance
Distributor audits performed by the company
procedures: Analyse sell-in versus sell-out data by distributor to identify stock building beyond normal cover.
Sample promotional claims and test for evidence the activity was performed, such as photographs, invoices or third-party verification.
Test credit exposure by distributor against approved limits and ageing.
Review the company's own distributor audit programme, coverage and follow-up of findings.
red_flags: Distributors with stock cover far above the network average
Claims supported by generic or reused evidence
Sales spikes before price increases
Distributor audits repeatedly deferred

risk: A product safety failure reaches consumers because quality controls at the plant are bypassed under production pressure.
audit_objective: Assess whether food safety controls operate as designed under real production conditions.
what_to_review: HACCP plan currency and critical control point monitoring
Deviations at critical control points and their disposition
Hygiene, pest control and allergen segregation
Supplier raw material approval and incoming testing
Certification audit findings and closure
procedures: Test critical control point monitoring records for completeness and for deviations released without a documented disposition decision.
Walk the plant during production and compare observed practice to the HACCP plan, particularly allergen changeover.
Trace incoming raw material batches to approved suppliers and required certificates of analysis.
Review third-party certification and regulator findings and verify corrective actions were implemented.
red_flags: Monitoring records completed in identical handwriting at one time
Deviations released "on management authority"
Allergen changeover cleaning shortened to hit output
Supplier approvals lapsed but deliveries accepted
evidence: HACCP plans and CCP monitoring records
Supplier approval files and certificates of analysis

subprocess: Asset Integrity and Safety Critical Maintenance
risk: Safety-critical network maintenance is deferred, raising the risk of asset failure, supply interruption and public harm.
audit_objective: Assess whether inspection and maintenance of safety-critical network assets is performed on schedule and defects are closed.
what_to_review: Asset criticality classification and inspection intervals
Overdue safety-critical maintenance by asset class
Defect close-out and interim risk mitigation
Vegetation management and third-party interference
Contractor competency for high-risk work
procedures: Extract the maintenance plan and quantify overdue safety-critical tasks by asset class and region.
Trace a sample of high-priority defects to closure and verify the remediation physically occurred.
Test whether deferrals were formally risk-assessed and approved at the required level.
Review contractor competency and authorisation records for high-voltage or high-pressure work.
red_flags: Deferrals approved in blocks at year end
Defects downgraded in priority without justification
Inspections recorded as complete with no field evidence
Contractors working outside their authorisation

risk: Customers in financial hardship or on medical support are disconnected or pursued in breach of regulatory customer protection obligations.
audit_objective: Confirm that customer protection obligations are applied before any restriction or disconnection.
what_to_review: Identification and flagging of vulnerable and life-support customers
Hardship programme access and affordability assessment
Pre-disconnection notification and cooling-off requirements
Debt collection agency conduct
Complaint and ombudsman case outcomes
procedures: Reconcile disconnections executed against the vulnerable and life-support customer registers; investigate any overlap.
Test that each disconnection followed every required notification step within the prescribed timeframes.
Sample hardship applications and test the timeliness and consistency of assessment.
Review ombudsman and regulator determinations and trace systemic causes to remediation.
red_flags: Life-support flags removed shortly before disconnection
Notification letters generated but not despatched
Hardship applications rejected at high rates by one team
Repeat ombudsman findings on the same issue

subprocess: Revenue Leakage Across the Order to Cash Chain
risk: Services are provisioned on the network but never reach billing, so the customer uses the service without ever being charged.
audit_objective: Quantify revenue leakage between provisioning and billing and assess whether revenue assurance detects it.
what_to_review: Reconciliation of network provisioning records to billing subscriptions
Free-of-charge and test accounts left active
Product catalogue consistency between systems
Discount and credit application
Revenue assurance coverage and independence
procedures: Reconcile active services on the network to active billing subscriptions; quantify the value of unbilled active services.
Extract free-of-charge, employee and test accounts and test whether each remains justified.
Compare product and tariff definitions across provisioning, rating and billing for inconsistencies.
Analyse credits and manual adjustments by user and reason code.
red_flags: Test accounts with genuine consumption
Long-lived free-of-charge accounts
Catalogue changes made in one system only
Credits concentrated with a small number of users

risk: A poorly controlled network change causes a major service outage, with regulatory reporting obligations and customer compensation following.
audit_objective: Assess whether network changes are controlled and whether resilience and recovery capability is proven rather than assumed.
what_to_review: Change approval, testing and back-out planning
Emergency change usage and retrospective approval
Single points of failure in core network
Disaster recovery and failover testing
Major incident reporting to the regulator
procedures: Sample network changes and test for approval, testing evidence and a documented back-out plan.
Quantify emergency changes as a proportion of all changes and test whether retrospective approval occurred.
Review the most recent failover or disaster recovery test and confirm it exercised a genuine failover, not a tabletop walkthrough.
Trace major incidents to root-cause analysis, regulatory notification within the required window, and corrective action closure.
red_flags: Emergency changes used routinely to bypass approval
Back-out plans stated as "restore from backup" with no detail
DR tests deferred or scoped to non-critical systems
Repeat incidents with the same root cause
evidence: Major incident and regulatory notification records
